title: Regional SLO boundary backpressure orchestrator and dynamic on-call flow
creator: Aisha Kapur
description: Implement an orchestration layer that ties regional SLO boundaries to automated backpressure controls, circuit-breaker triggers, and an adaptive on-call paging flow. The goal is to reduce noisy pages during transient capacity shifts while ensuring high-severity SLO violations escalate immediately and multi-region failover is executed predictably. This ticket covers: policy design, instrumentation, runbook authoring, PagerDuty/Slack automation, and a phased rollout with synthetic canaries.
acceptance_criteria: Region-level SLO breach detection emits a normalized severity event with context (affected routes, model variant, RTT percentiles, token rates)
Backpressure policy can be applied per-route and per-customer tier and reduces accepted QPS gracefully (configurable: 5%, 10%, 25%, 50%)
Circuit-breaker automatically trips when sustained error-rate or latency above threshold for configured window and triggers a controlled traffic shift to fallback region/variant
Pager noise reduced by >=40% on historical noisy alerts in the canary slice without masking high-severity incidents (measured over 2-week post-rollout)

Runbook automation posts a pre-populated incident play in Slack and, if severity >= Sev-2, escalates to on-call with a single actionable checklist; incident play contains links to traces, dashboards, and promoted mitigations
Playbook includes a safe rollback path and an automated metric check to verify that rollback restored SLOs within 30 minutes
tasks: Design policy schema for SLO-boundary -> backpressure mapping (PM/Eng co-owned)
Add telemetry enrichment: attach region, route, model_variant, batch_size distribution to SLO events
Implement backpressure controller in routing layer with graceful token-based shedding
Integrate controller with existing circuit-breaker service to coordinate tripping and half-open probes
Author runbook: initial triage, mitigation matrix, step-by-step region cutover, and rollback criteria
Build Slack/PagerDuty automation to create incident thread and attach runbook checklist
Create canary: 1% traffic slice, synthetic canaries, and dashboard for rollout monitoring
Run chaos experiment to validate controlled failover and rollback behavior
Add automated tests simulating transient latency spikes and validate no pages for minor blips
